items.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
items.excerpt: An MIT training technique trains climate emulators on deliberately unrealistic emissions scenarios, boosting accuracy and adaptability to unfamiliar futures while using only a fraction of the usual training data.

items.title: AI-written peer reviews outscored top human experts in blind comparisons, Harvard working paper finds
items.excerpt: In blind comparisons, both an AI judge and former journal editors preferred AI-written reviews of unpublished research papers over reviews by well-paid human experts in the large majority of cases.

items.title: After math, will AI upend science, too?
items.excerpt: Mathematicians will remember 2026 as the year AI changed everything about their field; Scientific American examines whether experimental sciences are next in line for disruption. Feature/analysis, not a new result.

items.title: AI improves cosmic particle scans to locate hidden objects more accurately in simulations
items.excerpt: University of Tartu and GScan built machine-learning models that combine straight-through and deflected muons for muon tomography; in simulations a hybrid method cut wrong merging of nearby hidden objects from about 15% to 2% (IEEE Access).

items.title: AI system can reconstruct aerodynamic shapes and predict their performance
items.excerpt: Kyushu University's PI-GAE, a physics-informed graph autoencoder, compresses wing and compressor-blade shapes into a few variables, rebuilding geometry within 0.3% and predicting performance (R² 0.946–0.992) without repeated CFD runs.

items.title: Preserving human involvement at the start of a creative task can improve AI-assisted outcomes
items.excerpt: In a PNAS Nexus experiment with 285 students, Wharton's Hosanagar and Ahn found ChatGPT cut story-writing time 36%, but stories were better only when humans kept ideation and outlining or had flexible AI help; merely approving AI drafts produced worse stories.

items.title: New AI tool exposes plant pathogens and the genes behind them
items.excerpt: Leiden University's bacLIFE machine-learning tool compares thousands of bacterial genomes to predict lifestyles such as plant-harming, and flags linked genes; knocking out six candidate genes made bacteria far less able to infect plants.

items.title: Independent technique validates landmark M87* image
items.excerpt: A CSIRO team used machine-learning and AI techniques to reanalyse the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope data and recovered a black-hole ring nearly identical to the original image, supporting that the ring is real rather than a processing artifact (Nature).

items.title: AI-generated molecular fingerprints help identify existing compounds with therapeutic potential
items.excerpt: University of Pittsburgh's FSGLD uses a GAN (DRUG-GAN) to generate molecular fingerprints, then searches databases for existing compounds that are novel relative to training molecules yet predicted to bind GPCRs and kinases (Science Advances).

items.title: Q-CTRL Demonstrates Push-Button Cold-Start Calibration on QuantWare Superconducting QPUs
items.excerpt: Q-CTRL's physics-informed AI state machine in Boulder Opal autonomously calibrated a 21-qubit QuantWare Contralto-D21 from an uncalibrated state to operational gate fidelities, detecting anomalies and recovering underperforming qubits.

items.title: IBM, Mitsubishi Chemical, and Keio Train Generative Quantum Eigensolvers on 70-Qubit Hardware
items.excerpt: IBM Quantum, Mitsubishi Chemical, Keio and NVIDIA trained transformer-based Generative Quantum Eigensolver policies directly on the 156-qubit ibm_kobe processor and applied them zero-shot to simulate organic molecules with up to 70 qubits (arXiv).

items.title: QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic Use AI to Reduce Quantum Circuit Resource Requirements
items.excerpt: New research from QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic shows AI can cut quantum circuit resource requirements through automated circuit design and optimization. Note: similar framing to the 11-11 DeepMind resource-reduction card; deprioritized.

items.title: Researchers Explore Quantum Inspired AI Repair
items.excerpt: QDeep and ITMO University developed Tree-Ising, a quantum-inspired Ising-optimization method that repairs repetitive reasoning loops in small language models.

items.title: Teaching AI to build better enzymes
items.excerpt: SynFit, an open-source ML tool from UCSB and Georgia Tech, learns several enzyme traits at once from small datasets; lab tests on a carbon-boron-bond-forming cytochrome c produced many variants hitting both high yield and high selectivity.

items.title: AI agents advance atomic modeling and reveal how aluminum nanoparticles oxidize
items.excerpt: Tohoku University's MLP Copilot, a human-in-the-loop multi-agent framework, built machine-learning interatomic potentials from quantum calculations and showed how an oxide shell throttles or, when ruptured, accelerates aluminum nanoparticle oxidation (PNAS).

items.title: Using Vibrations and AI, Future Robotic Missions Could Handle Buried Rocks Autonomously
items.excerpt: Virginia Tech researchers combine vibration sensing with AI to estimate the depth of buried objects, a step toward lunar and Martian robots that can handle subsurface rocks autonomously.
